slots.label: Heading 1
slots.default: IT support in Manchester: frequently asked questions

slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Not covered here? Ask us directly — same working day response.

slots.label: Question 1
slots.default: Do you have an office in Manchester?

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: No. Our offices are at 124 City Rd in London and Caxton Point in Stevenage, and we would rather say so than list a virtual address in Manchester. The city is covered by our UK service desk plus field engineers who travel to customer sites. Most issues never need a visit: we respond the same working day and resolve most issues remotely. When a visit is requested we aim to have an engineer with you the same working day.

slots.label: Question 2
slots.default: You support MBKB Group in Manchester. What does that involve?

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: MBKB Group is a training provider with more than 140 staff, and we set up their IT as well as supporting it day to day. It is a good illustration of the usual shape of our work: a growing organisation with no large internal IT team, needing the fundamentals to be dependable rather than clever.

slots.label: Question 3
slots.default: Can you cover multiple sites across the North West?

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: Yes. Multi-site works best with one service desk and one set of standards rather than each location improvising, so monitoring, patching and security are consistent everywhere and an engineer is sent to whichever site needs someone physically there.

slots.label: Question 4
slots.default: How do onsite visits actually work?

slots.label: Paragraph 5
slots.default: Most problems are solved remotely and fast, which is why site visits are the exception rather than the rule. When something needs hands on the hardware, a failed switch, a machine that will not boot, a move or a fit-out, one of our field engineers travels to you and we aim for the same working day.

slots.label: Paragraph 6
slots.default: Faults are graded P1 to P5, each with its own SLA. P1 means the business cannot operate, a total outage or a dead server, and gets immediate attention. Everything below still carries a committed response time, so lower-priority tickets are not left to drift.
